# Eryri National Park adventure, sports and outdoor activity ideas

While a walk up Yr Wyddfa is a great achievement, you can get so much more exhilaration out of your trip to Eryri National Park. It's crammed full of exciting activities to get the blood pumping - which will you try first?

SaveShare

Eryri is truly one of the most extraordinary corners of Britain. This beautiful part of Wales has towering mountains and a wild coastline, offering every kind of outdoor activity, wet or dry. There are also brilliant beaches, lovely old towns, and lots to do in this area for an unforgettable family adventure holiday.

## Explore Eryri's mountains

We start in the [Carneddau and Glyderau](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/carneddau-and-glyderau) in the heart of the mountains. Here in the Ogwen Valley, Tryfan is the spur on which Edmund Hillary trained for Everest in 1953 and with stamina and nerves of steel, you can stand on its vertiginous summit after two hours. Teenagers love climbing [Tryfan](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/visit/wales/carneddau-and-glyderau/walking-and-climbing-on-tryfan), partly because it looks like a giant stegosaurus at the side of the A5! A note of caution though, Tryfan is technical in nature and should only be tackled by experienced mountaineering families, or with a guide. From a car park by the lake, pick up the path by Gwern Gof Uchaf farm but please be mindful of [parking responsibly](https://eryri.gov.wales/visit/plan-your-visit/parking-in-snowdonia/) whilst visiting this area.

![Waterfall in the Ogwen Valley with Tryfan in the background](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-06/cw-c145-1819-0021%20small.jpg.jpg.webp?itok=rRRQllRL)

[Cwm Idwal walk](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/carneddau-and-glyderau/trails/cwm-idwal-walk) is just as rewarding, but requires far less effort! Starting from the car park at the far end of Llyn Ogwen, after a stiff 20-minute ascent you will reach Cwm Idwal, a glacial lake ringed by peaks fit for an Arthurian blockbuster. Afterwards, drive into the U-shaped Nant Ffrancon valley for the most beautiful glacial geography lesson in Wales.

![Walkers on a stone path leading to a lake surrounded by mountains.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/James%20Nee%20-%20Cwm%20Idwal%201.jpg.webp?itok=KvGzk6V)

Cwm Idwal, Eryri, North Wales

View Credits

© James Nee

It's the most famous walk in Wales as well as the highest mountain – everyone should experience the thrill of standing on the summit of Yr Wyddfa at least once in their lives. If you're up for a challenge, you could take on the climb as part of the [Snowdonia Trail Eryri Marathon](https://alwaysaimhighevents.com/events/snowdonia-trail-marathon-eryri) in July. Being one of the UK's most challenging trail races, the marathon and ultra marathon options aren't for the faint-hearted but there's always the half marathon and 10K options!

Walking to the summit is no mean feat either. Choose your challenge from the [six routes to the top](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3070), most of which are manageable for all the family if you’re all reasonably fit. However, we wouldn’t recommend the famous Crib Goch arête, which is more advanced. Make sure you take heed of the [Eryri National Park safety advice](http://www.snowdonia.gov.wales/visiting/safety-advice) before heading out. For families who aren't experienced, [Edge of Wales Walk](https://www.visitwales.com/product/916068) provide bespoke walking holiday packages to meet individual requirements.

You don’t actually have to walk to reach the top of Yr Wyddfa - you can take the [Snowdon Mountain Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/516165). It runs all the way to the summit over the summer and part of the way, to Clogwyn, during winter. The path to the top is open all year, if conditions allow, so experienced climbers can follow the path from Clogwyn to the summit. Here the [Hafod Eryri visitor centre](https://snowdonrailway.co.uk/the-experience/#summit-visitor-centre) opens from late Spring to October, so you can enjoy a well-earned cup of tea along with brilliant views all the way to Ireland on clear days.

There are plenty of other family-friendly peaks to choose from in and around Eryri. [Cader Idris](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5019) is another beauty, an extinct volcano that looms up between the twin estuaries of the rivers Dyfi and Mawddach.

[Aberdyfi](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1948733) – ‘aber’ means ‘mouth of a river’ (Aberdovey)– is a classy fishing village that marks the southern edge of Eryri's coastline. From here, it heads north through family-friendly resorts [Tywyn](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5455) and [Abermaw](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1959973) (Barmouth), past Mochras, also known as [Shell Island](https://www.visitwales.com/product/958731) whose beach, as the name implies, is a great place to enjoy the splendour of its shells.

## Climbing in Eryri

Another way to explore is through climbing and where better to enjoy the sport than Sir Edmund Hillary's training ground. Accredited activity providers can provide beginners with taster sessions or short courses.

[Search for climbing activity providers](https://www.visitwales.com/search?search=snowdonia&location=&lat=52.9005518&long=-3.8963384&radius=80450&unit=miles&sliderValue=5&subfilter%5B0%5D=Climbing&sector%5B0%5D=Activity)

In the shadows of Yr Wyddfa, slabs in the Llanberis Pass beneath are a cradle of British climbing. Accredited operators like [RAW Adventures](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1889604) will show you the ropes (literally) and provide a primer in mountain safety. Alternatively, [park at Pen-y-Pass](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/snowdon/pen-y-pass-car-park/) to ascend the highest peak in Wales and England. The return trip on the Miners’ Track or Pyg Track is at least five hours.

![Walker on a mountain overlooking a lake.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2020-05/nvw-c147-1819-0104%20small.jpg.webp?itok=mXA0lFLP)

## Hang out at Zip World or hit the bike trails

Once the world's largest slate quarry, Penrhyn Quarry, near Bethesda is now home to the longest zipwire in the northern hemisphere at [Zip World Penrhyn Quarry](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1446056). [Velocity 2](https://www.zipworld.co.uk/adventure/velocity) is the fastest in Europe, reaching speeds of over 100mph - hurtling down the mile-long wire 500ft above a lake, it's the nearest thing to flying.

![](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/oembed_thumbnails/IFGoQ9l6Y9g0a0px5dsQP2z9w1LaLLfu2NKYE0447iA.jpg)

Zip World Velocity, North Wales

For a shared outdoor adventure, continue south to [Coed y Brenin](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1971405). Welsh royalty once hunted in King’s Forest, but now families can hit the trail in Wales’ mountain bike mecca, with bike hire and family-friendly trails.

Mountain bike trails are also available at [Antur Stiniog](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1471647), Llechwedd, which caters for all abilities dependent on your riding skills!

![Three cyclists on bike track with sunset ](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2023-09/JB_WINTER_ADVENTURE_HIGHRES_2520.jpg.webp?itok=8W3UoTxD)

Antur Stiniog, Blaenau Ffestiniog, North Wales

## Catch air at Bounce Below

Nearby, deep inside the Zip World Llechwedd complex, which is also home to [Zip World Caverns](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1561448), in a massive underground chamber, there’s the world’s most extraordinary bouncing experience - [Bounce Below](https://www.zipworld.co.uk/adventure/bounce-below). Three huge trampolines have been set up, one above the other, in a space that’s like an alien cathedral, all connected with slides and ladders, and lit by psychedelic multi-coloured lights.

![People bouncing on underground trampolines.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__2_1x/public/media-library/2020-06/NVW-C04-1415-0129-small.jpg.webp?itok=tjVawKMm)

## Test your bravery at Go Below Xtreme

If you’re a fan of zip lines and underground attractions, then you will love the Go Below Xtreme experience at [Go Below Underground Adventures](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1889644). Located in an old Victorian slate mine near Blaenau Ffestiniog, 1,300ft down in the ground, it's the longest and deepest underground zip ride in the world! Featuring nine zip lines and 14 traverses, it’s a personally guided extreme underground challenge, finished with a 70ft free fall jump. Scary stuff for an exhilarating adventure activity.

See how former professional rugby player and outdoor enthusiast [Chris Knight took on the Go Below Xtreme](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6212) experience on an epic underground adventure.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B5pNQyzgku5/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

## Pick up a paddle

It’s striking how quickly the landscape softens as you leave the central National Park towards [Y Bala](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3258) (Bala). The River Tryweryn tumbles down in Eryri's National Park eastern foothills, canopied by oaks and home to more otters than anywhere else in Wales. Your best chance to see one is at the [National White Water Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/926700) on a Tryweryn Safari. It’s a lovely trip, slipping through the lower Tryweryn Valley for 3.7 miles (6 km) on a family-friendly adventure. A dam releases the water, rapids fire and everyone whoops down a short whitewater rollercoaster. Book in advance and bring spare underclothing for your wetsuit and a towel for a shower.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B2cTlqBhTt8/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

There's also opportunities to paddle at [Llyn Padarn](https://www.visitsnowdonia.info/padarn-country-park) near Llanberis beneath the steep cliffs of its old slate mines, nudging onto lovely beaches. The grander [Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake)](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/llyn-tegid/) is Wales’ largest natural lake, four miles long with the narrow gauge steam trains of [Llyn Tegid \| Bala Lake Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/528332) travelling along its banks in summer. The beautiful Llyn Gwynant near Beddgelert also attracts many kayaking enthusiasts, and offers great outdoor activities for all of the family against a backdrop that was a location for Hollywood blockbuster _Tomb Raider 2_.

Afon Conwy, Afon Glaslyn and Afon Llugwy also provide white water opportunities for the experienced kayaker. The shores of Eryri are packed with sea kayaking possibilities and experienced instructors at [Snowdonia Watersports](https://www.visitwales.com/product/930412) have a range of exciting options to develop your paddle skills, from sea kayaking to white water.

## Go off-road with Snowdonia Safaris

You’ve walked, climbed and paddled. It’s high time someone else did the hard work so that you can enjoy the scenery. The experienced guides at [Snowdonia Safaris](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1887573) can give you the 'lowdown' with their insider information and offer a range of road trips to suit your interests, with tours including 'Lost Quarries and Villages' and 'Tombs and Views'. Being the passenger will give you time to 'drink in' the horizon-busting panoramas of peaks. Speaking of which, there are few better ways to round off a mid-summer activity break than with a stop-off at the pub!

## Canyoning in Eryri

Eryri, with its deep gorges and mountain terrain, is ideal for a canyoning adventure. This adrenalin-fuelled activity can be experienced with qualified guides who will provide full safety briefings to safeguard the adventure seeker, whilst ramping up the fun.

## Be safe!

Exploring the outdoors is fantastic fun, but please read up on the risks and make sure you are prepared.

- Follow the [safety advice for exploring Wales' National Parks](https://www.visitwales.com/node/2923) and these [tips for staying safe on the Welsh coast](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3897).
- Visit [AdventureSmart.uk](http://www.adventuresmart.uk/) for information on how to stay safe whilst exploring Wales.

# Ogwen

[Home](https://eryri.gov.wales/)

[Visit](https://eryri.gov.wales/visit/)

Ogwen

The breathtaking valley of Ogwen

The valley of Ogwen is one of the National Park’s most breathtaking backdrops. The valley is a great base for exploring both the Carneddau and Glyderau mountain ranges and is home to Cwm Idwal—a jaw-dropping glacial valley famous for its geology.

Getting to Ogwen

![](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/alert.svg)

**Before you visit**

Double yellow lines have been placed along parts of the A5 in Ogwen. Parking is not permitted on double yellow lines at any time including on the side of the road and the pavement.

At busy times, such as the spring and summer holidays, parking spaces in Ogwen fill up quickly. You should use bus services from Bethesda if parking spaces in Ogwen are full.

By public transport

Using public transport is a convenient way to get to the Ogwen valley.

**T10 TrawsCymru Bus Service**

The TrawsCymru T10 service links Bangor, Bethesda and Betws y Coed and stops at Ogwen.

[T10 Bus Timetable (Traws Cymru)](https://traws.cymru/en/services/BARB/T10)

Where to park if using public transport

The best place to park if you’re using public transport to get to the Ogwen valley is at the local football club at the nearby village of Bethesda.

**Bethesda Football Club Parking** Fee: £7/day paid by pay and display machine

Public transport services stop at bus stops in Bethesda.

Two 22kW community EV chargers are now on site, but a parking fee still applies.

Please note that the gate to the car park is closed overnight from 22:00 to 07:00, although overnight charging is permitted.

[View Bethesda Football Club Car Park on Google Maps](https://goo.gl/maps/dhiSPFhjCZJ3Qegf6)

Go green

**Bws Ogwen Electric Bus Service** The Bws Ogwen service is part of the Ogwen Partnership scheme—a social enterprise working for the benefit of the economy, environment and communities of Ogwen.

The 9-seater bus travels between the nearby village of Bethesda and Ogwen.

It’s possible to park at Bethesda Football Club and catch the Bws Ogwen service from the bus stops in the village.

Bethesda Football Club Parking Fee: £7

[View Bethesda Football Club Car Park on Google Maps](https://goo.gl/maps/dhiSPFhjCZJ3Qegf6)

[Bws Ogwen Timetable](https://www.facebook.com/bwsogwen)

[Ogwen Partnership Website](https://www.partneriaethogwen.cymru/en/)

By car

Parking is limited at Ogwen and spaces fill up quickly, particularly during peak times.

There is a small car park owned and managed by the National Park Authority at the Ogwen Centre.

**Ogwen Centre Car Park**

Daily rate (Expires at midnight): £6.00

4 hours: £3.00

Blue badge/disabled parking: 2 spaces

EV charge points available

_Payment method ‘Chip and pin’ or contactless only. Cash payments not accepted._

[View on what3words](https://w3w.co/simulations.deform.weekday)

[View on Google Maps](https://goo.gl/maps/Uj2yRLr3YJoLQY2e8)

Cwm Idwal Centre

At the heart of the Ogwen valley is the Cwm Idwal Centre with ample facilities such as:

- Interactive exhibition

- Public toilets and showers, accessible 24 hours a day

- Ogwen snack bar providing a range of drinks, snacks, pasties and a variety of locally-baked cakes


Cwm Idwal Partnership Officer’s Headquarters, the Eryri National Park Authority wardens work from here on occasion. However, due to the nature of warden work, the presence of a warden cannot be guaranteed during core hours.

Ogwen Cottage

Ogwen Cottage has long been familiar to climbers, ramblers and general visitors to Ogwen for many years. The National Trust bought the property back in 2014 and the Glyderau and Carneddau wardens are based here.

The Outward Bound Trust also has a centre here which they use as a great location for challenging and adventurous outdoor learning courses for children and young adults.

[Ogwen Cottage (National Trust website)](https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/ogwen-cottage)

Walks and Routes

Cwm Idwal Walk

Follow the route around the breathtakingly unique, Cwm Idwal.

[Cwm Idwal Walk](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/cwm-idwal/)

![Cwm Idwal with clouds forming above with some blue sky](https://eryri.gov.wales/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/JHM-SNP-CWM-IDWAL-3-of-87.jpg)

Outstanding geology

The Ogwen valley is home to a rich geological history stretching over millions of years.

[Eryri's Geology](https://eryri.gov.wales/discover/landscapes-and-wildlife/geology/)
